| Prioritize replenishment, identify weak products   |
| Raw material supplier | Supplier reliability, stock availability, lead times, open orders         | Identify shortage risk, improve procurement        |
| Service provider      | Open work orders, resolution time, SLA compliance, technician utilization | Prioritize jobs, rebalance technician workload     |

The shell, account management, analytics infrastructure, AI framework and memory integration can be shared. The sidebar, page structure, KPI definitions, operational records, filters, charts and executable actions must be domain-aware.

### 5\. How to execute this without repeating the same debugging cycle

Do not ask Copilot to rewrite the entire repository in one enormous operation. Give it the master prompt above, then enforce these checkpoints.

### Implementation checkpoints

0 of 6

1. Quick scan

Inspect the actual code, dependencies, routes, data sources, duplicate services and tests.

Audit report exists and identifies real files and defects.

2. Data integrity

Remove silent synthetic fallbacks, fix tenant isolation, verify MongoDB access and protect dangerous endpoints.

Tests prove empty data and service failures do not fabricate results.

3. Five-domain UI

Build distinct workspaces with domain-specific navigation, metrics, pages and responsive layouts.

All five domains render different, semantically correct workspaces.

4. Real AI and memory

Connect verified operational evidence to the configured LLM and real Hindsight recall.

Evidence and memory references are traceable; failures are explicit.

5. Actions and learning

Execute supported actions, measure actual outcomes and retain verified experiences.

An end-to-end action can be traced from baseline to outcome and memory.

6. Regression verification

Run builds, automated tests, and end-to-end checks; document anything unverified.

Actual command results and remaining gaps are recorded.

### 6\. The final test that matters most

The project should demonstrate one complete, evidence-backed business scenario—not just five attractive dashboards.

For example, in the distributor domain:

* MongoDB contains actual shipment records for a specific area and time window.

* LOGIMIND calculates the area's delivery delay rate and average delivery duration.

* Hindsight recalls a genuinely retained, relevant prior experience—or reports that no relevant memory exists.

* The LLM produces a recommendation supported by current records and any recalled experience.

* The user approves a supported dispatch or agent-allocation action.

* The backend executes the action and records the change.

* New operational observations become available for outcome measurement.

* LOGIMIND evaluates whether performance improved, declined or remains inconclusive.

* Hindsight retains the verified experience only when the action and outcome meet the defined requirements.

* A future analysis can retrieve that experience and show its provenance.

If no new operational observations have arrived, the outcome remains pending. The application must not invent a better delivery time to complete the demonstration.

Once this vertical slice works, repeat the same shared intelligence lifecycle through restaurant, retail, raw-material supplier and service-provider adapters, each with its own real data model and valid actions.

Final principle: LOGIMIND's competitive advantage should come from its ability to understand five kinds of businesses through one reliable intelligence platform—not from the number of screens, files, seeded memories, or AI-generated recommendations in the repository.
